name: Cloven Hoof
summary: Deep in Thousand Needles, the Galak centaur guard the Cloven Hoof at Splithoof Hold. Tauren scholars at Freewind Post seek to learn what its strange energy reveals.

sections.title: A Sacred Centaur Relic
sections.body:
At Splithoof Hold, the Galak centaur keep the Cloven Hoof in an ancient brazier. Magical fire surrounds it, and blessed water must quench the flame briefly before anyone can handle the relic. The centaur clans are divided and violent, yet their care for the brazier points to a ritual bound to their origins.

At Freewind Post, Rau Cliffrunner and other tauren observers hope the hoof's strange aura will teach them about the centaur who have long troubled Kalimdor's plains.

faq.q: Where is the Cloven Hoof kept?
faq.answer: The Cloven Hoof rests in an ancient brazier at the back of Splithoof Hold, a cavern in Splithoof Crag north of Freewind Post. Elite Galak warriors guard it.

faq.q: Why does Rau Cliffrunner want the Cloven Hoof?
faq.answer: Rau Cliffrunner wants to study the Cloven Hoof to learn about centaur origins and magic. He senses strange energy from the relic and hopes it will reveal hidden truths about the hostile clans.

faq.q: How is the Cloven Hoof retrieved from the brazier?
faq.answer: Magical fire surrounds the Cloven Hoof, so it cannot be taken directly. Pour a phial of special water into the ancient brazier to quench the sacred flame briefly, then take the hoof before the blaze returns.

faq.q: Who are the Galak centaur guarding it?
faq.answer: The Galak are a centaur tribe that holds the northern reaches of Thousand Needles. Their stronghold is Splithoof Crag, where they fiercely guard their sacred fire from outsiders.

angles.text: For generations, the nomadic tauren have endured relentless centaur aggression. Learning the origins and magic of relics like the Cloven Hoof could teach you about their old adversaries.
Ritual elements can briefly quench magical flames and let you retrieve the Cloven Hoof. Such work calls for careful spiritual study in Kalimdor.
